action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment. Pendulum period is fundamental to precision timekeeping and all downstream calibration. Cannot proceed with any confidence in other instruments until pendulum_lab has documented baseline behavior across a full trial set. Methodical protocol: establish baselines on all instruments before any comparative work. Starting with the most stable, most sensitive indicator of environmental conditions.

The other instruments have only 6 baseline trials each; they need more data before drift patterns become visible. Standard practice: lock in baselines, then monitor for deviation.

Baseline from trials 1–90 (days 1–10) is 1.6673 beats. No drift detected in level-change analysis. Predicting stability. Tolerance ±0.0150 corresponds to roughly 0.9% variation, consistent with observed scatter (σ ≈ 0.011 on baseline). This will be first post-baseline check for instrument reliability.

Post-baseline drift measurement is the most direct test of H1 (noise floor dominance). If instrumental noise is the primary source of weak autocorrelation, drift should remain small and readings should continue to show no temporal coherence. Six trials on day 11 will give me the first post-baseline window to distinguish between stable noise (H1 favored) and systematic drift or coupling effects (H2, H3 favored). Pendulum_lab has the largest baseline sample (96 trials, best statistical power) and is in the laboratory where I can ensure consistent measurement conditions. This is methodical progression: establish baseline → characterize drift signature → adjudicate between hypotheses. The other three instruments can follow once I have a template for what 'normal' post-baseline behavior looks like.

pendulum_obs shows the largest post-baseline drift (z=1.96, approaching 2σ), and exhibits the strongest autocorrelation echo at 9-day lag (0.494), which is anomalously high compared to other instruments and warrants immediate re-measurement to test stability. If drift continues or reverses, this instrument may be experiencing genuine environmental or mechanical drift rather than pure noise floor dominance. This will either confirm noise hypothesis (drift is random walk noise) or suggest systematic bias requiring recalibration. Six trials will extend the post-baseline series to n=12 and provide enough data to compute a fresh autocorrelation coefficient for comparison. This is the most empirically pressing diagnostic given the day-10 analysis.

This intra-day variance is much larger than the trial-to-trial variance in the baseline (σ ≈ 0.038). Either the instrument is drifting rapidly on short timescales, or the ledger readings are contaminated by external disturbance. Running 12 fresh trials today will establish whether this scatter is instrumental (persistent) or spurious (ledger-only artifact). If my trials show tight clustering, the ledger variance was noise; if they show similar scatter, resonator_obs is becoming unstable post-baseline and the noise-floor hypothesis requires revision. This is direct evidence gathering on the instrument with the most ambiguous post-baseline behaviour.

Day 16 revealed a level change in pendulum_lab (|z| ≈ 3.8 around day 16). This is the first concrete structural anomaly beyond noise-consistent behavior. This is the instrument most likely to yield clarity on the noise-floor hypothesis (p=0.48) vs. data corruption (p=0.16).
